references.text: God promises Abraham to give the land to his descendants – the first promise of the land of Canaan to the patriarchs.
God repeats the promise to Abraham that the entire land he can see will be given to him and his descendants forever.
God promises Abraham the whole land of Canaan as an eternal possession for him and his descendants – the same promise here renewed to Jacob.
God renews the land promise to Isaac and confirms the oath He swore to Abraham, promising to give all these territories to his offspring.
At Bethel, God promises Jacob the land on which he lies, to him and his descendants – the same place where the promise in chapter 35 is renewed.
Jacob recounts to Joseph how God at Bethel promised to give this land to his descendants as an eternal possession.
Deuteronomy confirms and actualizes the promise given in Genesis by calling for the taking of the land that was sworn to the fathers.
Exodus 6:8 shows how the individual promise in Genesis becomes a national reality for the children of Israel at the Exodus.
Genesis 28:13 is the original revelation of the land promise to Jacob, which is confirmed and renewed in 35:12.
Ezekiel confirms that the eternal land promise from Genesis still applies to the restored nation.
Isaac's blessing links Jacob's reception of the land directly back to Abraham's original promise.
Moses' final words confirm that the land promise given to the patriarchs is the unshakable foundation for Israel's ownership.
Moses uses the promise of the land and descendants from Genesis as a theological argument in his intercession.
